stem.text: An estimate of the consumption function of an economy is given by an equation C = 10 000 + 0.8Y where C = consumption and Y = income.
Which conclusion can be drawn from this information?

options.text: The average propensity to consume is constant.
The average propensity to consume increases as income increases.
The average propensity to consume is always equal to the marginal propensity to consume.
The average propensity to consume is always greater than the marginal propensity to consume.

points.text: APC = C/Y = 10000/Y + 0.8; MPC = dC/dY = 0.8. Since 10000/Y > 0 for all Y, APC = MPC + 10000/Y > MPC always

explanation.text: The marginal propensity to consume (MPC) is the slope of the consumption function — the coefficient on Y, which is 0.8, a constant. The average propensity to consume (APC) is total consumption divided by total income, C/Y = (10000 + 0.8Y)/Y = 10000/Y + 0.8. Because the 10000/Y term is always positive (and shrinks toward zero as Y grows, but never reaches it), APC is always strictly greater than MPC (0.8), though the gap narrows as income rises.

optionAnalysis.text: APC = 10000/Y + 0.8 is not constant — it falls as Y rises, since the fixed 10000 is spread over a larger income.
APC decreases, not increases, as income rises, because the autonomous 10000 component becomes a smaller share of a larger income.
APC equals MPC only if there is no autonomous consumption (i.e. the intercept were 0); here the intercept is 10000, so APC always exceeds MPC by 10000/Y.
APC = MPC + 10000/Y, and since 10000/Y is always positive for positive income, APC is always greater than the constant MPC of 0.8.

reasoningChain: Identify the marginal propensity to consume as the coefficient on Y in the consumption function: MPC = 0.8 (constant).
Derive the average propensity to consume: APC = C/Y = 10000/Y + 0.8.
Compare APC to MPC: APC − MPC = 10000/Y, which is always positive for Y > 0, so APC > MPC always, and APC falls toward (but never reaches) MPC as Y grows.

inferredMistakes.text: Confusing the behaviour of APC with MPC, assuming that because MPC is constant, APC must also be constant, without separately calculating C/Y which includes the autonomous consumption term.

bullets: Option B was the most common incorrect answer.

This suggests that most candidates were not familiar with the concept of the consumption function. Due to the marginal propensity to consume being less than 1 (in this case, 0.8), as income increases, consumption will increase by a smaller proportion. This means that the average propensity to consume will decrease as income increases.
